read: full (abstract, introduction, related work, section 3 on BBH's limits, section 4 on construction, section 5 results and analyses, conclusion, pp1-12; appendix A task descriptions skimmed, pp17-34)
venue_now: Text is arXiv:2502.19187v2, 6 May 2025 (p1 footer; '(c) 2025 Google DeepMind'); no venue is printed. The May reference list gives ACL 2025 (Volume 1: Long Papers), pp. 26473-26501, which this file cannot confirm.
what_it_is: BIG-Bench Extra Hard (BBEH), a general-reasoning benchmark that replaces each of BBH's 23 tasks with a harder task probing a similar skill (pp1-2; p6 Table 1). It was built because BBH had saturated, with state-of-the-art models above 90% accuracy (p1, p3). Tasks were hardened semi-adversarially until two Gemini reference models scored below 70% (p5); some are generated by programs (e.g. Boolean Expressions, p18; Zebra Puzzles, p33) and others adapted from existing datasets. Scoring is automatic and deterministic on the final answer and summarised by an adjusted harmonic mean; the best general-purpose model reaches 9.8% and the best reasoning model (o3-mini high) 44.8% (p1; p8; p9 Table 2).
domain: general reasoning (logic, temporal, spatial, causal, humour, arithmetic, algorithms)
size: 23 tasks of 200 questions each, except Disambiguation QA with 120 (p5), i.e. 4,520 items (my count); BBEH Mini of 460 (p7); 12 models evaluated, from Llama 3.1 8B to o3-mini (high) (p8; p9 Table 2)
source_of_items: mixed: tasks adapted from existing datasets (e.g. Linguini, SpatialLLMEval, SportQA, Test of Time), tasks generated by programs, and 120 author-written Disambiguation QA items (p6 Table 1; p18; p21; p33)
instances: static (a fixed released set, although several tasks were produced by generators)
has_gold_traces: no (two tasks ask the model to find the first error in a given reasoning trace, Dyck Languages and a Word Sorting subtask, but these are scored on the final answer; p6 Table 1)
evaluation: final answer, automatic and deterministic (p2); adjusted harmonic mean over tasks as the headline, micro average also reported (pp8-9)
human_validation: Disambiguation QA only: 120 items written by ten author-annotators, each checked by a second annotator with adjudication; 25 items were revised (p21). No human baseline for the benchmark.
contamination_measures: none stated; the benchmark is released publicly on GitHub (p1). Its answer to saturation is difficulty, not secrecy.

engtrace_use.sentence: First, static benchmarks like Glue (Wang et al., 2019) and BBH (Kazemi et al., 2025) are increasingly prone to model saturation (Ott et al., 2022) and data contamination (Deng et al., 2024); ... (L97-105)
engtrace_use.explanation: 'BBH (Kazemi et al., 2025)' attributes BIG-Bench Hard to this paper, which introduces a different benchmark, BIG-Bench Extra Hard (p1). BBH is Suzgun et al. (suzgun2022bbh). As an example of a saturating benchmark BBEH is the opposite: it was designed for headroom, with best harmonic-mean accuracies of 9.8% and 44.8% (p1, p8). The paper is, however, direct evidence for the claim about BBH: 'the rapid advancements in LLM development has led to a saturation of BBH, with state-of-the-art models achieving over 90% accuracy' (p1), 'causing BBH to disappear from the latest model evaluation reports' (p3).

suggested_wording: BIG-Bench Hard (Suzgun et al., 2022), on which state-of-the-art models now exceed 90% accuracy, has been replaced by the harder BIG-Bench Extra Hard (Kazemi et al., 2025).
facts_to_cite: BBH has saturated: state-of-the-art models exceed 90% accuracy, which 'renders BBH less effective in discriminating' between the latest models (p1); BBH has disappeared from recent model evaluation reports (p3).
BBH's limits included high random-chance baselines (8 of 23 tasks binary and 5 more with at most five options), shortcuts, short inputs (about 700 characters on average) and few reasoning hops (p3).
BBEH replaces each of BBH's 23 tasks with a harder task probing a similar skill (p2; p6 Table 1), with 200 questions per task and 120 for Disambiguation QA (p5).
Tasks were hardened semi-adversarially until two Gemini reference models scored below 70% accuracy (p5).

Scoring is automatic and deterministic; the headline adjusted harmonic mean is 9.8% for the best general-purpose model (Gemini 2.0 Flash) and 44.8% for o3-mini (high) (p2; p8; p9 Table 2); the corresponding micro averages are 23.9% and 54.2% (p9).
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares deterministic final-answer scoring and some program-generated tasks, but releases one fixed public set. Two tasks test finding errors in a given reasoning trace (p6 Table 1), a skill adjacent to EngTrace's step verification, yet BBEH neither supplies gold traces nor scores the model's own steps. No engineering content, no private pool, no expert validation of an evaluator.
notes: The May reference entry has six wrong given names, confirmed against p1: Mehran (not Mostafa) Kazemi, Bahare (not Behnam) Fatemi, Chrysovalantis (not Christos) Anastasiou, Sanket Vaibhav (not Shweta V.) Mehta, Lalit K. (not Lovish K.) Jain, Virginia (not Valentina) Aglietti. The abstract's 9.8% and 44.8% are harmonic means, while the introduction's 23.9% and 54.2% are micro averages (p2 against p9), so quote the metric with the number. Caution for the revised Introduction: BBEH's answer to saturation (harder items) is not EngTrace's, and EngTrace's own answer scores reach 0.970 (state brief section 4); cite BBEH for BBH's saturation, not as a model for EngTrace.
